title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt — the annual revision edition that folds in the end-June survey benchmark, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,180 bytes) by the tic-annual-survey-prelim-2027-02-26 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2027 table's June row reads '30' in the column headed 'Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt', alongside '16' in the Monthly and Quarterly-derivatives columns, under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. The same page's notes state 'Quarterly U.S. Gross External Debt. The time of release is normally at 4:00 p.m. in Washington D.C. The release dates are the last business day of each quarter (March, June, September, and December)' and, in the same block, 'Revised data for the previous five quarters (back to the first quarter of the previous year) are normally released on the last business day of June. Revisions include the results of the Survey of Foreign Holdings of U.S. Securities at end-June of the previous year.' Corroborated mechanically: 2027-06-30 is a Wednesday and the last business day of June 2027, offset +0 from the page's own stated rule. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and because this is a distinct series from the annual survey the proposer owns. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-annual-survey-prelim-2027-02-26 initial research (2026-09-09), and this entry is the whole reason that research changed its mind about where the survey benchmark actually goes. The proposer was itself proposed on the premise that the annual survey is what makes February/March MONTHLY vintages the largest restatements in the TIC panel. That premise is half impossible: the February monthly release publishes on the 11th business day plus 0-3 days and the survey on the last business day of the same month, a gap of at least 7 calendar days computed over every February from 2003 to 2050, so no February monthly vintage can ever contain the survey. And Treasury's note (d) puts the survey-into-March convention in the past tense — 'Before September 2011... usually released in March to include preliminary data from the annual survey' — replaced for Major Foreign Holders by note (c)'s Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct schedule since December 2011. THIS release is the one feedback path Treasury still documents in the present tense, in the sentence quoted in the source field above. It therefore belongs on the calendar as the destination of the survey's benchmark, and it is the observation that would settle whether the March monthly restatements the sibling ledgers measured are the survey at all or something else. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds: 16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is a quarter stale, and no house playbook is macro-keyed. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
